definition: the state of being dormant or delayed until conditions allow activity
memoryTip: Latent stage — hidden or idle until something triggers it.
correctPassage: There is often a latency between infection and the appearance of symptoms.
wrongPassages: The latency of the fireworks display meant the sky lit up the instant the switch was flipped.
She measured the drawer labeled latency and found only pens and spare batteries inside.
His latency attendance meant he never missed a single class all year.

definition: develop slowly under favorable conditions; keep warm to hatch or grow
memoryTip: Like eggs in an incubator — grow slowly under steady care.
correctPassage: The startup will incubate new ideas before seeking outside investment.
wrongPassages: They hoped to incubate the scandal by leaking it to every outlet at once.
She incubated the walkout by locking the doors and cutting badge access mid-meeting.
He tried to incubate the rumor by demanding an immediate public retraction.

definition: combined effect greater than the sum of the parts
memoryTip: Syn + energy: working together multiplies the power.
correctPassage: The merger was sold on the promise of synergy between the two product lines.
wrongPassages: Working alone, she produced more synergy than the entire committee combined.
The rivalry created synergy by ensuring the two teams never shared data.
Each department claimed synergy while refusing every joint project on the calendar.

definition: wary and careful; unwilling to take unnecessary risks
memoryTip: Circum-spect: look all around before you step.
correctPassage: Lawyers advised a circumspect response until more facts were known.
wrongPassages: His circumspect dive off the pier ignored every posted warning about the rocks.
A circumspect investor poured the entire savings account into a single unvetted tip.
She gave a circumspect answer that named names and promised results by Friday.

memoryTip: Without guile (tricks) — open, honest, nothing up the sleeve.
correctPassage: His guileless manner made colleagues trust him quickly.
wrongPassages: The guileless con artist ran three aliases and a fake charity for years.
Her guileless contract buried the fees in footnotes no customer would read.
A guileless witness changed the story three times and denied knowing the defendant.
